instruments.evidence: The socket payloads, read from real dialled connections: group_member_joined {conversation_id, user_id} for a direct add and for an accepted invite (two inputs; the accept path had no test -- finding 1); group_keys_shared {conversation_id} to the newcomer after a share and after a rotation that carries history.
Event names are group_member_joined and group_keys_shared; 3b must use these exact strings. broadcastToGroup already sends group_member_muted and friends the same way.
Payload fields conversation_id and user_id, as the tests read them.

instruments.why: No untyped accessor on the server side.

instruments.evidence: The tests drive the real routes (add, invite + accept, share, rotate) and read the real hub's frames, as a client receives them.
Sibling membership events: mute and ban already broadcast through broadcastToGroup; removal and leave do not need a key event (the next sender rotates).
announceJoin and announceShared return early on a nil hub (the handler unit tests pass nil); every other branch is reached by the socket tests.
broadcastToGroup logs a failed participant query; the join itself has already committed, so a missed announcement costs only the backup path, and the read-side share in 3b covers it.

instruments.why: announceJoin reuses broadcastToGroup rather than a second member loop.

instruments.evidence: Every INSERT INTO conversation_participants for a group: CreateGroup (the first members, no history yet), AddGroupParticipant and AcceptGroupInvite -- both announce. The rest are mod mail. Every writer of older-version copies: Rotate with history and ShareHistory announce group_keys_shared; GrantInviteHistory and GrantAddedMemberHistory give copies to the joiner, who is told through group_member_joined, which reaches every member including the joiner -- 3b must drop the joiner's own remembered-missing versions on that event.
The two new socket tests pass under -race.
Both announcements run after the transaction commits, so a rolled-back join announces nothing.
